goals: Define a safe, dependency-aware pruning plan for exact Enderscape 3.0.2 on Minecraft Java 26.2 Fabric without weakening retained End biome, structure, Magnia, potion, or Matcha Flavoured behavior.
Suppress future acquisition and discovery of owner-selected equipment while retaining registry identities needed by existing worlds and inventories.
Reconcile every Enderscape food and food-like loot path with exact Matcha Flavoured component-bearing identities without changing Enderscape's original loot odds or counts.
scope: Audit the exact Enderscape 3.0.2 binary, built-in resource/data packs, recipes, loot tables, advancements, tags, structures, configured and placed features, mixins, and decompiled gameplay code.

Trace mirror, dagger, rubble-shield variants, Shadoline armor, Enderscape enchantments, native food/effect loops, Matcha-sensitive vanilla food loot, and the full Magnia system through acquisition, discovery, save-data, and worldgen dependencies.
Record the narrowest safe future implementation boundary and an owner-decision checklist; do not implement pruning, build a Canary, deploy, or claim Minecraft runtime evidence in this audit task.

exclusions: Enderscape source or binary modification, registry removal, mixin changes, data/resource-pack implementation, generated artifact production, Canary identity, deployment, or acceptance.
Minecraft launches, runtime observations, Test Slot or Test Instance Manager changes, and any access to protected or retired gameplay profiles.
Changes to originals, WORKBENCH_SERVER_STATE.json, Matcha Flavoured, Matcha x JEI Integration, Enderscape's upstream repository, or any unrelated Workbench project.
Claims that static decompilation proves runtime safety, or that disabling a built-in pack retroactively changes already-generated chunks or stored item/effect identities.
